Pleiades (M45) - S50 Pro, 70min (60s subs), Bortle 4

These are the famous "Seven Sisters" of our night sky and they carry with them one of the oldest and most fascinating legends in history. According to Greek mythology, they were the daughters of the Titan Atlas and the nymph Pleione. When Zeus condemned Atlas to eternally bear the weight of the heavens upon his shoulders, his daughters were left defenseless. The giant hunter Orion became infatuated with them and began pursuing them relentlessly for seven long years.

In despair, the sisters pleaded with the gods for help. Moved by pity, Zeus first transformed them into doves so they could escape capture, and then turned them into stars, setting them within the constellation Taurus. Yet celestial mechanics made this pursuit eternal: upon his death, Orion was also turned into a constellation and placed in the sky right behind the cluster. Even today, night after night, the hunter seems to chase the seven maidens from east to west.

There is, however, a fascinating detail: when observing the Pleiades with the naked eye, most of us can clearly make out only six stars. The Greeks created the myth of the "Lost Sister" to explain this anomaly: it is said that Merope, the only sister to marry a mere mortal (King Sisyphus) instead of a god, perpetually hides her face in shame, making her star the faintest and hardest to see.

Beyond the myth, M45 is a breathtaking astrophysical spectacle: a group of very young stars passing through a cloud of cosmic dust. This dust reflects their intense light, creating the wonderful blue draperies that envelop the cluster.
